operator_io_quirks: Mixed-case identifiers: tables 'captain'/'Ship', columns 'Captain_ID','Ship_ID','Built_Year','Class','Rank' — must be double-quoted with original spelling; column lookup case-insensitive.
Tiny tables (captain 7 rows, Ship 9 rows) — no sampling cap needed; original_values are full columns.
FK captain.Ship_ID -> Ship.Ship_ID, parent exists and is unique PK; child distinct=5 < parent 9, so FK draw with replacement will create duplicate Ship_IDs in captain (allowed, not unique).
captain.age declared TEXT but stores numeric-looking strings ('40','54') — String fuzzer, not Number; int-like strings get +1/-1 variants.
Ship.Built_Year declared REAL, storage real, values 1997.0/1998.0 — dispatches to Number(scale=4) with float perturbation +-0.01/+-0.02, not Date.
Ship.Type has distinct=1 ('Panamax') — String sampler with single element; fresh draws still possible via p.
Ship.Class and captain.Class share name but are unrelated (no FK); literal pool anchors by column name will merge them across tables.
captain.Rank contains comma ('Commander, junior captain') — String contaminate/prefix/suffix will mangle; no quoting issue since values are bound params.
No NOT NULL, no CHECK, no UNIQUE constraints beyond PKs — TS will not enforce anything in Python; only PK/unique dedup applies.
Both PKs are single-column INT (Captain_ID, Ship_ID) — max_l0 = inf for these, so fresh draws unbounded.
Ship_ID appears as PK in Ship and as FK in captain — same column name, different roles; pool seeding must not conflate.
No views/triggers/indexes in DDL; empty clone is just the two CREATE TABLEs.
operator_ts_expectations: Number fuzzer on Captain_ID/Ship_ID: uniform ints in [-10^4,10^4] (scale=4 default for INT? actually int family scale from args, none -> default), then +-1/+-2 perturbation; PK dedup keeps first occurrence.
Number fuzzer on Built_Year (REAL): floats in [-10^4,10^4] perturbed +-0.01/+-0.02 — wildly implausible years (e.g. -3000.5) drive FN on year-range predicates.
String fuzzer on Name/Type/Class/Flag/Rank: random a-zA-Z0-9() strings length 0-20, plus 5 original samples, plus pool literals; contaminate 50% — implausible names drive FN on LIKE/equality.
String fuzzer on age (TEXT): random strings, not numbers — queries comparing age numerically will mostly miss (FN) or match spuriously (FP).
FK captain.Ship_ID drawn from Ship.Ship_ID final values with replacement — ties/duplicates in captain.Ship_ID are common; queries with DISTINCT/COUNT(DISTINCT) may FP.
Ship.Type single distinct value: TS may produce many distinct random strings, so 'Type=Panamax' predicates FN; conversely fresh strings rarely equal.
Table sizes: choose_table_sizes gives 1+30u for level 0 (Ship) and x4 for level 1 (captain) capped 2500, or rand_lin 30+200u — captain can be much larger than 7, Ship larger than 9.
PK dedup on Captain_ID/Ship_ID after generation shrinks rows; with max_l0=inf fresh draws, dedup rarely triggers for small n.
Pool literals from train SQL (e.g. 'Frigate','Panama','KR') get mixed with random strings — some plausible values survive, some don't.
Missing ties: original captain has 5 distinct Ship_IDs over 7 rows (duplicates exist); TS with replacement also duplicates, so join-count queries may accidentally match.
FP risk: random strings over charset include digits/parens, so numeric-looking text (age) may accidentally satisfy comparisons.
No Date/Time/Bool fuzzers triggered — no text-stored dates in this DB.
